title: Make the output parse every time
brief: A downstream parser breaks on one malformed response in a thousand. Decide how much structure to demand from the model, and whether the schema belongs on the answer or on a tool call.

blocks.title: From a polite request to enforced schemas
blocks.intro: Each step buys more guarantee and more rules to follow.

options.name: Prompt only
options.summary: Ask for JSON in the instructions and parse what comes back.
pros: Works on any model and API
cons: No guarantee of valid JSON or the right fields
options.bestWhen: Prototypes and cases where a retry is cheap.
options.avoidWhen: A production parser sits behind the call.

options.name: JSON mode
cons: Only valid JSON is guaranteed, not your schema [[r8]]
options.bestWhen: You need JSON but the shape is loose or the model lacks schema support.
options.avoidWhen: Specific fields and types must be present.

options.name: Structured outputs
pros: Safety refusals are detectable in the response
cons: Azure limits are tighter than OpenAI's [[r33]]
options.bestWhen: The model's final answer must match a schema.
options.avoidWhen: Your schema needs features outside the supported subset.

options.name: Strict function calling
options.summary: Tool arguments follow your schema. The model decides when to call and your code runs the function.
pros: Natural fit for actions and lookups
cons: Reasoning plus tools has API-specific limits
options.bestWhen: The model should trigger an action or fetch data.
options.avoidWhen: You only want a formatted final answer, where structured outputs is simpler.

rows: `text.format` `{type: "json_schema", strict: true, schema}` in Responses, `response_format` in Chat [[r8]].
Up to 5,000 object properties and 10 nesting levels. Names and enum values total at most 120,000 characters. At most 1,000 enum values.
Up to 100 object properties and 5 nesting levels.
Not compared here. Read the Claude page.
`pattern`, `format`, `minimum`, `maximum`, `minItems`, `maxItems` supported, but not on fine-tuned models.
Read the Claude page for limits.
Every field required (emulate optional with a union with `null`). `additionalProperties: false` is mandatory. Root is an object, not `anyOf`.
`auto`, `any`, `tool` or `none`. `any` and `tool` return 400 on Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1, and with manual extended thinking [[r50]].
`parallel_tool_calls: false` gives zero or one call. Strict works with parallel calls on non-fine-tuned models since 2025-05-20 [[r12]].
Docs say structured outputs are not supported with parallel calls, so set `parallel_tool_calls` to `false`.
From GPT-5.4, Chat does not support tool calling when effort is not `none`. GPT-6 Astra and 6.1 Sol need Responses for tools [[r6]].
`gpt-5.6-sol` fails with "Function tools with reasoning_effort are not supported" even when effort is omitted [[r15]].

blocks.title: The function calling loop
blocks.alt: The app sends tool schemas to the model, the model returns a function call, the app runs the tool, returns the output with the call id, and the model answers.
blocks.src:
sequenceDiagram
  participant App
  participant Model
  participant Tool
  App->>Model: Request with tool schemas
  Model-->>App: function_call with arguments
  App->>Tool: Run the function
  Tool-->>App: Result
  App->>Model: function_call_output with call_id
  Model-->>App: Final answer
blocks.caption: Your app always runs the function. On GPT-6, `async: true` lets the model keep reasoning while the tool runs, and you return the result with the original `call_id` [[r2]].

blocks.title: Structured output in Responses
blocks.caption: Illustrative. `priority` is optional in spirit, but strict mode needs it required, so it is a union with null.

blocks.caption: Illustrative. Responses replaces `response_format` with `text.format` [[r6]].

blocks.title: The same schema on Claude
blocks.code:
msg = client.messages.create(
    model="claude-sonnet-5-5",
    max_tokens=1024,
    messages=messages,
    output_config={"format": {"type": "json_schema", "schema": ticket_schema}},
)
blocks.caption: Illustrative. Strict tool use is a separate switch: `strict: true` on the tool definition [[r32]].

items.symptom: The parser fails on a rare malformed response
items.cause: Prompt-only and JSON mode do not enforce your schema.
items.fix: Move to structured outputs or strict tools, and alert on parse failures so you see the rate.

items.symptom: A refusal sentence arrives where JSON should be
items.cause: A safety refusal replaces the schema output, and OpenAI makes refusals detectable in the response [[r8]].
items.fix: Check for a refusal before parsing and route it to a safe fallback.

items.symptom: A schema that works on OpenAI returns 400 on Azure
items.cause: Azure allows 100 properties and 5 nesting levels, and lists `minLength`, `maxLength`, `pattern` and `format` as unsupported.
items.fix: Flatten or split the schema, drop the keywords, and test on the Azure deployment.

items.symptom: The model skips the tool or picks the wrong one
items.cause: `tool_choice` is `auto`, so the model may answer directly. On Claude Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 a forced `any` or `tool` returns 400.
items.fix: Use `required` or a named function on OpenAI. On those Claude models use `auto` with strict tools or structured outputs, and improve the tool descriptions.

items.symptom: Tool arguments are schema-invalid from a fine-tuned model
items.cause: A fine-tuned model that makes several calls in one turn loses strict mode [[r9]].
items.fix: Validate arguments in your code and retry, or avoid parallel calls with that model.

blocks.title: Sources disagree on strict plus parallel calls
blocks.md: OpenAI's changelog says strict mode works with parallel tool calls on non-fine-tuned models since 2025-05-20 [[r12]]. The Azure page still says structured outputs are not supported with parallel function calls [[r33]]. Follow the page for the platform you deploy on, and test.

quiz.q: This schema is sent to OpenAI with `strict: true`. What is wrong with it?
options: Strict mode needs an array at the root of the schema
`type: "string"` is not allowed anywhere in strict mode
Nothing, since optional fields are allowed in strict mode if they are left out of `required`
Fields must all be required, and `additionalProperties` must be `false`
quiz.explain: Strict mode needs all fields in `required` and `additionalProperties: false`, and optional values are emulated with a union with null. The root must be an object, not an array, and string types are fine.

quiz.q: Select every statement that is true for structured outputs on Azure OpenAI as of 2026-10-13.
options: It allows up to 100 object properties and 5 nesting levels
Limits match OpenAI's 5,000 properties and 10 levels
Docs advise `parallel_tool_calls: false` with structured outputs
quiz.explain: Azure documents 100 properties, 5 levels, those unsupported keywords and the advice to disable parallel calls. The root cannot be `anyOf` on either platform, and the OpenAI limits are far higher than Azure's.

quiz.q: A service uses Chat Completions with function tools on GPT-5.4 or later at reasoning effort `medium`, and tool calls start failing. Which change is most justified?
options: Use Responses, or set effort to `none` where allowed
Raise `max_completion_tokens` so the tool call has more room
Switch from strict mode to JSON mode for the arguments
Add a `seed` so that the tool call repeats reliably
quiz.explain: From GPT-5.4, Chat Completions does not support tool calling when effort is not none, so the API surface or the effort must change. A larger cap, JSON mode or a seed do not change that rule.

takeaways: JSON mode guarantees valid JSON only. Structured outputs and strict tools guarantee your schema
Schema limits and keywords differ sharply between OpenAI and Azure, so test on the platform you deploy
Check for refusals before parsing, and validate arguments from fine-tuned models
Reasoning plus tools pushes you to Responses on GPT-5.4 and later
